judgments.rationale: Under clause (iii), only the parent's agreement under clause (i) is explicitly required to be in writing. The source text does not require the local educational agency's agreement to be in writing, so adding a requirement that both parties agree in writing introduces an unsupported legal obligation.

The definition of the IEP Team in 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(B) specifies the required and discretionary members of the team. Nothing in the source text requires prior written parental consent for team members to participate; the written agreement and consent rules under clause (iii) govern excusals from attendance rather than general membership or participation.

Clause (iii) directly governs clause (i) by mandating that a parent's agreement that attendance is not necessary shall be in writing. Incorporating this condition into the summary accurately reflects the full statutory requirements for the attendance exemption while preserving the correct modal force and scope.

Clause (iii) explicitly dictates that parental consent under clause (ii) shall be in writing. Adding this statutory condition to the summary faithfully represents the full requirements for excusal without distorting the permission modality or neighboring duties.

Under clause (D), an invitation to the subchapter III representative is required 'at the request of the parent.' The statute does not impose a requirement for written parental consent for this invitation, and the written consent requirement of clause (iii) applies only to excusals under clause (ii).

Under clauses (ii) and (iii), excusal requires both the written consent of the parent (and consent of the agency) and the member's submission of written input prior to the meeting. These are separate conjunctive conditions; the member's written input does not satisfy or replace the requirement for written parental consent.

source_spans.quote:
(ii) Excusal A member of the IEP Team may be excused from attending an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, when the meeting involves a modification to or discussion of the member’s area of the curriculum or related services, if—

(I) the parent and the local educational agency consent to the excusal; and

(II) the member submits, in writing to the parent and the IEP Team, input into the development of the IEP prior to the meeting.
A parent’s agreement under clause (i) and consent under clause (ii) shall be in writing.
